items.title: Trafigura Snaps Up Copper in Asia as China Faces Supply Crunch
items.author: Julian Luk, Jack Farchy and Alfred Cang
items.content: <article>Trafigura Group has been buying large volumes of copper to boost sales into Asia as local supplies run low, adding to a scramble for metal that’s pushed regional premiums for spot cargoes to record highs.</article>

items.title: Why India’s Stock Markets Hold a Session on Diwali: Explainer
items.author: Samie Modak
items.content: <article>India’s stock markets will open for a special shortened session on Sunday as the country celebrates Diwali, its biggest festival, keeping alive a tradition that has survived the shift from handwritten ledgers and bustling trading floors to smartphones and algorithms.</article>

items.title: China Extends Gold-Buying Streak to Two Years as Prices Drop
items.author: Yihui Xie
items.content: <article>China’s central bank added to its gold reserves in October — extending a buying streak to two years — as the precious metal fell almost 7% to end the month below the $4,000-an-ounce support threshold.</article>

items.title: Beijing Vows to Hit Back Against US Sanctions on China Companies
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>China strongly opposes US sanctions on two Chinese companies over their dealings with a third party and reserves the right to take “necessary measures” to protect its interests, China’s Ministry of Commerce said on Saturday.</article>

items.title: The Corner Store Brings Its New York Experience to the Las Vegas Strip
items.content: <article>Catch Hospitality Group is opening a Las Vegas location of The Corner Store at the Cosmopolitan. Co-Founder and Partner Eugene Remm says the 150-seat restaurant will preserve the intimacy and authentic SoHo experience of its 75-seat New York original, rather than offer a Vegas-specific or watered-down version. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Elanco Shares Jump After Q3 Beat and Outlook Raise
items.content: <article>Elanco Animal Health shares rose nearly 8% after the company reported third-quarter earnings above expectations and raised its full-year outlook. Jeff Simmons, Elanco’s President and CEO, called it a high-quality quarter, citing 11% reported growth and broad strength across markets and product lines. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Kailey Leinz on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Sweetgreen CEO Says Sales Rebound After Cyclospora-Related Traffic Drop
items.content: <article>Sweetgreen CEO and Co-Founder Jonathan Neman says that sales momentum has improved after a summer Cyclospora outbreak—unrelated to Sweetgreen’s stores but damaging to traffic across the sector. The company reported October comparable sales growth of about 5%, following a return to flat comps in September, and saw further improvement in early November. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Kailey Leinz on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: FIGS Beats Earnings as Demand Outstrips Supply, CEO Trina Spear Says
items.content: <article>FIGS reported third-quarter top- and bottom-line results above expectations, with revenue of $190.7 million versus an estimate of $182.8 million. The company logged a fourth consecutive quarter of at least 25% revenue growth; non-scrubwear revenue rose 35%, and international revenue also increased. CEO and co-founder Trina Spear said health care professionals are expanding their FIGS purchases beyond scrubs to items such as underscrubs, compression socks and outerwear, for work and off-duty wear. She speaks with Romaine Bostick & Kailey Leinz on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: AI-Generated Movie Heading Theaters
items.content: <article>Artificial intelligence is moving from experimental videos to the big screen. Fable Studio CEO Edward Saatchi says a team of just 30 people spent nine months creating Gods Don’t Give Gifts, an AI-generated animated feature that still relies on human directors, writers, voice actors and artists. He joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss how AI changes the filmmaking process and what it means for Hollywood's traditional production model. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Providing Capital to Tech Companies: Masters In Business with Ann Berry
items.content: <article>Barry speaks with Ann Berry, founder and managing partner of Threadneedle. They discuss her path from Goldman Sachs M&A and private equity to running a hospitality services company through the pandemic. They also discuss Ann's early-stage bets on AI and deepfake detection, and surveying the expanding IPO landscape. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Airbnb Surges 12% as Growth Accelerates and Outlook Rises | Closing Bell
items.content: <article>Comprehensive cross-platform coverage of the U.S. market close on Bloomberg Television, Bloomberg Radio, and YouTube with Romaine Bostick, Kailey Leinz, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Hedge Funds Fled Bullish Oil Bets Ahead of Election Day Drop
items.author: Lorelei Smillie and Mia Gindis
items.content: <article>Hedge funds cut bullish crude bets by the most since June as the US and Iran struck rare de-escalatory notes, positioning them to profit from the selloff after the Democratic sweep of Congress.</article>

items.title: Wall Street Grapples With $5.7 Trillion Rout as AI Bets Unwind
items.author: Justina Lee and Lu Wang
items.content: <article>Months of unease over Wall Street’s artificial-intelligence boom erupted into a global market convulsion this week, opening a dangerous new chapter for the investment frenzy that has helped power stock prices, corporate spending and economic growth.</article>

items.title: Retail Traders Cautiously Buy Stocks After Worst Rout Since 2025
items.author: Jessica Menton and Felice Maranz
items.content: <article>Retail traders, the stock market’s most avid dip buyers since the pandemic, were among the investors buying on Friday after US equities had their worst day since 2025. But their typical enthusiasm was nowhere to be found.</article>

items.title: Braskem Owners Pull Funding Offer as Debt Talks Hit Snag
items.author: Mariana Durao and Giovanna Bellotti Azevedo
items.content: <article>Talks between Brazil’s Braskem SA and its creditors regarding an out-of-court debt rework have soured, with shareholders taking a proposed capital injection key to a deal off the table if talks stand as they are, according to people familiar with the matter.</article>

items.title: Canadian Dollar Notches Worst Week Since September on Weak Jobs
items.author: Melos Ambaye
items.content: <article>The Canadian dollar posted its biggest weekly loss since late September after weaker-than-expected domestic employment data reinforced concerns about the outlook for the country’s economy.</article>

items.title: How a Bank Scandal Is Taking Down Trump’s Ally in Paraguay
items.author: Manuela Tobias and Ignacio Olivera Doll
items.content: <article>Officials at the Inter-American Development Bank’s investment arm suspected something was off almost as soon as they walked through the doors of Paraguay’s Ueno Bank SA.</article>

items.title: Gold Extends Drop on Stronger-Than-Expected US Employment Data
items.author: Jack Ryan and Preeti Soni
items.content: <article>Gold fell after a hot US nonfarm payrolls print added fuel to speculations that the Federal Reserve will seek to raise interest rates to contain inflation.</article>

items.title: Chip Stocks Climb After Rout, But AI Doubts Linger: Markets Wrap
items.author: Rita Nazareth
items.content: <article>A rebound in chipmakers propped up the stock market as dip buyers emerged despite economic data that reinforced speculation the Federal Reserve will boost rates in December.</article>
